result:
I reviewed migrate-run and the verdict is **DONE**: nothing is Critical and nothing needs fixing now. The work is one commit, `9920c24`, the same one the implementer reported. It only changes test step definitions so they match the feature wording that was reworded (`e963f03`) before the work-item was claimed. Nothing under `features/` or `scripts/` changed.

I ran the 26 migration-tools tests: all pass. `tools check` found 15 ruff issues, all on lines older than this commit; vulture is clean, and the project has no import contracts. I did not run the whole suite, so the report's suite totals are unchecked.

- **F1 (Important, observation):** one assertion is gone. The test that a moved record keeps an `about` it already has was deleted along with its feature line, and the plan doesn't list the removal. The code (`with_id` in `scripts/migrate_layout.py`) still keeps it, so nothing is broken today. But nothing would catch it if that changed. Getting it back needs a new scenario line from the formulator, since the feature is read-only here.
- **F2 (Minor, observation):** the new "has the content … apart from …" step ignores any `id:`, `kind:` or `about:` lines, not just the ones r9 and r12 should add. It would pass even if `records/logs/r1.md` were wrongly given an id. Today that file comes through unchanged, so it doesn't matter yet.
- **F3 (Minor, drop):** the work-item's `fileset:` is out of date. It doesn't list the two step modules this commit changed.
- **F4 (Minor, drop):** the 15 ruff issues; none is on a line this commit added.

The plan is out of date too: it covers r1–r11 while the work-item accepts r1–r12. So the r12 and reworded r2/r11 test changes have no plan decision to check against; the findings file lists this under "Cannot verify".
